symptoms_observed: Yellowing and drying of leaves starting from the tips
Brownish, circular 'hopper burn' patches spreading outward
Small brown insects visible at the base of the plant
treatment_steps: Drain water from the field for 3-4 days to reduce the hopper population.
Open 30 cm alleyways after every 2-3 metres of planting to improve airflow.
Stop urea top dressing until the infestation subsides — excess nitrogen worsens outbreaks.
Count hoppers per hill; if more than 10, contact your Krishi Vigyan Kendra before any chemical spray.
organic_options: Encourage natural enemies: mirid bugs and spiders control planthoppers — avoid broad-spectrum insecticides.
Neem oil spray (5 ml per litre) at the plant base can suppress early-stage populations.
safety_note: Do not apply insecticide mixtures without confirmation from your local Krishi Vigyan Kendra. This tool never recommends chemical dosages — an expert must confirm them.
